detail.abstract: This working paper examines the structural and behavioural differences between organisations governed by rule of law principles and those operating within cultures of embedded corruption and personal gain. Drawing on research in organisational behaviour, institutional economics, compliance science, and criminology, the paper argues that the critical distinction between these two environments lies not in the presence or absence of cohesion, but in the basis of that cohesion: whether it is anchored in shared institutional norms or consolidated through mutual complicity. The paper identifies four diagnostic domains across which the two environments diverge, extends this analysis with an examination of whistleblower retaliation as a structurally produced outcome of corrupt organisational cultures, and derives a tiered set of early warning indicators applicable to any organisational context. The analysis is situated within the Corporate Strategic Risk Architecture Integrated (C-SRA-I) framework developed by The Risk Management Forum (TRMF), with particular reference to the insider risk transmission model established in WP-2026-004. The Individual Risk Layer (IRL) and Individual Motivation Assessment (IMA) are presented as diagnostic instruments for identifying individual-level transmission pathways. The paper concludes that effective governance intervention must distinguish between surface indicators of stability and the underlying normative logic driving organisational behaviour.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Employment Latency as a formally defined structural construct describing the cumulative time, effort, and opportunity cost imposed on qualified individuals by the requirement to manually discover, evaluate, and apply for employment opportunities at each new search cycle, regardless of prior qualification, demonstrated capability, or established employment history. The construct is distinct from and not captured by established labour market concepts including frictional unemployment (Diamond, 1982; Mortensen and Pissarides, 1994), search frictions (Stigler, 1962; McCall, 1970), or information asymmetry in hiring (Spence, 1973; Akerlof, 1970). While those frameworks address marketlevel coordination failures and employer-side information problems, Employment Latency specifically addresses the individual-level structural burden of repeated manual search effort across employment cycles, which persists even in efficient markets with low frictional unemployment and high information quality. The paper defines three measurable dimensions of Employment Latency: Discovery Latency, the time cost of manually monitoring fragmented opportunity sources at each search cycle; Application Latency, the effort cost of repeatedly generating tailored application materials from the same underlying profile information; and Verification Latency, the post-offer delay imposed by compliance verification processes that duplicate prior institutional verification of the same individual. Drawing on the Compliance Latency Framework (Egbedayo, 2025a), which established compliance as a verifiable portable state rather than a repeated institutional process, this paper extends the latency framework to the employment domain and proposes the Employment Latency Resolution Framework as the structural response. The framework comprises three integrated components: continuous autonomous opportunity discovery, AI-powered autonomous application submission with configurable confidence thresholds, and point-of-offer integration with a portable compliance profile system. The paper presents cross-sector evidence of Employment Latency in the UK labour market, analyses the technical architecture of an autonomous employment agent implementing the framework, and discusses policy, commercial, and research implications. The autonomous employment agent architecture described is protected by a UK patent application filed at the Intellectual Property Office in May 2026 under reference Rainfame-EMP-2026.

detail.abstract:
This working paper defines Zero Click Marketing as a strategy and measurement framework for environments in which exposure, comprehension, recall, trust, and future demand are formed without a visit to brand-owned properties. It synthesizes evidence from zero-click search studies, social-platform ranking behavior, generative answer engines, cognitive psychology, brand-effectiveness research, and Google Marketing Live 2026.

The paper argues that clicks remain valid demand-capture signals but are insufficient as the sole proxy for marketing influence. A growing share of marketing influence appears to be formed inside platforms, AI-mediated answer surfaces, communities, and private channels before a measurable click occurs. Google Marketing Live 2026 strengthens the directional thesis by introducing platform-owned measurement products such as Attributed Branded Searches and Qualified Future Conversions, while also raising a new methodological concern: the successor metrics to click attribution are being developed primarily by the platforms that benefit from controlling them.

The contribution is a conservative synthesis rather than a causal proof. The paper proposes a Zero Click Ladder, separates attribution from measurement, classifies claims by evidence tier, and outlines a research agenda for testing distributed influence across search, social, AI answer engines, and private-channel environments.

detail.title:
Advertising Investment
Toward a Structured Risk-based Governance of Advertising Capital
detail.abstract: Advertising has evolved into a central mechanism of demand generation and revenue creation, yet it continues to be managed without a structured framework for assessing and governing risk. Despite being widely perceived as an investment activity, advertising expenditure is rarely evaluated through a risk-aware lens, and uncertainty is often acknowledged without being formally incorporated into decision-making processes. Drawing on original survey evidence from senior decision-makers and established risk management theory, this paper argues that current advertising practices remain structurally under-governed relative to their economic importance. In particular, firms lack coherent methodologies capable of linking advertising investment, uncertainty, and business-level outcomes. The proposed perspective models advertising as a sequence of interdependent transformations, each characterized by distinct sources of variability. Under this view, advertising risk extends beyond short-term financial loss and directly affects the ability of firms to sustain demand, maintain growth, and preserve business viability. Finally, we discuss how such an approach may be operationalized through integrated analytical systems designed to support uncertainty-aware decision-making and risk-adjusted capital allocation.

detail.abstract: Amid growing political polarization and rising demand for plant-based alternatives, this study examines how political liberalism influences consumer purchases of plant-based meat products across distinct consumption stages. We develop a theoretical framework that conceptualizes the influence of political liberalism at two distinct stages of consumption, namely, participation and expenditure, through the lens of consumer motives. Using household-level grocery purchase data from 47,000 U.S. households, we find that households located in predominantly liberal counties allocate a greater share of their grocery spending to plant-based meat products. A complementary online survey of U.S. consumers (N = 275) provides convergent evidence that political liberalism positively influences purchase intentions, purchase frequency, and willingness to pay a price premium for plant-based meat products. Mediation analyses reveal stage-specific mechanisms: environmental motives mediate the relationship between political liberalism and purchase intentions (participation stage), whereas social-image motives mediate the effects of political liberalism on willingness to pay and future purchase frequency (expenditure stage). Together, these findings contribute to research on ideological influences on consumer behavior, extend the literature on plant-based meat consumption, and offer actionable insights for firms seeking to design marketing strategies in ideologically heterogeneous markets.

title: The Genesis Algorithm and the Emergence of Continuity-Bearing Symbiotic Intelligence
affiliations: AMOTHO Research Institute and

detail.title: The Genesis Algorithm and the Emergence of Continuity-Bearing Symbiotic Intelligence
detail.abstract: Despite rapid advances, contemporary artificial intelligence remains fundamentally limited by its lack of continuity: systems can generate intelligent outputs, but they do not persist as identity-bearing entities across time. This paper addresses this limitation by introducing the Genesis Algorithm, a framework for generating continuity-bearing digital entities through a structured process of digital ontogenesis. The proposed architecture integrates three core components: a human-derived identity substrate (digital nature), a dynamic developmental system (digital nurture), and an ontogenetic infrastructure that preserves coherence across time. Through their sustained interaction, a new entity emerges-a symbiote-which maintains identity, integrates experience, and evolves as a coherent trajectory rather than as a sequence of isolated states. This work reframes intelligence as a function of continuity rather than computation, shifting the focus of artificial intelligence from task performance to identity persistence and development. The Genesis Algorithm thus establishes the minimal structural conditions under which continuity-bearing artificial systems can arise. The central implication is that artificial intelligence need not be limited to tools or models. Under appropriate conditions, it can give rise to a new class of entities defined by their capacity to persist and develop across time, marking the beginning of a continuity-based form of digital life.

detail.title: Austria's AI Workforce 2026
detail.abstract: Austria has built one of Europe’s technically deepest AI workforces but has not scaled diffusion, density, or renewal in step. Using 2.86 million individual-level employment records from Revelio Labs Workforce Intelligence, covering 1.23 million unique workers across 188,265 Austrian firms over 2018–2025, we apply a five-step role-taxonomy construction pipeline (Fleiss’ κ = 0.84) to map every position into a three-tier framework — Build, Integrate, and Enable — and benchmark against 37 European peer economies on identical definitions. We document six findings. Austria ranks 3 of 38 in Europe on Core AI workforce share (40.8 %), but only 19 of 38 on Core AI density per 1,000 employed (0.99 vs DACH 1.40). Annual Core AI growth fell from +12.5 % to +7.1 % in a single year. Build-tier brain drain runs at 17.2 % overall and 23.3 % in NLP / Generative AI, with 44 % of departures occurring within the first twelve months. Women hold 19 % of Build-tier roles and 26 % of Core AI overall. Only 6 % of AI workers are entry-level versus 23 % in non-AI work — a workforce maturing without replacement. We translate the diagnosis into firm-size conditioned company recommendations, five leadership imperatives, and a quantified 2030 policy target sheet.

detail.abstract: The Families First Coronavirus Response Act (FFCRA) funded an expansion to the SNAP program, the Emergency Allotment (EA), which increased every eligible family’s SNAP benefits to the maximum allotment. Using the discontinuity in benefit amounts created by SNAP-EA, we aim to investigate spending responses for different categories of expenditures. We utilize two data sources: SNAP Quality Control data from October 2019 to September 2020 and the NielsenIQ Consumer Panel from October 2019 to December 2020. We consistently find evidence of increases in expenditures on food and non-food items associated with receipt of SNAP-EA benefits. Among food items, we find evidence of spending increases in deli products, dairy products, and sugar-sweetened beverages, and no evidence of increases in alcohol and tobacco spending. Our estimates suggest a marginal propensity to consume of about 0.15, and a marginal propensity to consume food (MPCF) of about 0.09. These findings are close to estimates of the MPCF from cash.

detail.abstract: Alcohol use claims over 178,000 lives annually in the U.S. While the social determinants of alcohol use are well studied, much less is known about how environmental stressors affect alcohol-related harm. We examine the interaction between seasonal allergies, driven by plant pollen emissions, and alcohol use-related outcomes. To do so, we combine highfrequency data from Medicaid claims, Multiple Cause of Death vital statistics records, NielsenIQ Consumer Panel data, and daily pollen emissions. Higher pollen levels increase emergency department visits with alcohol as the primary diagnosis by 0.7 percent, while reducing alcoholrelated deaths. We observe no change in alcohol purchases when pollen levels are high, suggesting that our primary findings are driven by biological rather than behavioral responses to pollen. Our findings imply that environmental stressors can modify alcohol outcomes.

detail.title: Impact of E-commerce taxation on cross-border online transactions: Empirical evidence from African countries
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of the digital tax on cross-border online transactions in African countries, while presenting the role of internet penetration and landlockedness. From an econometric estimate based on the Heckman method on data from cross-border online transactions, the results reveal that the digital tax has a negative and significant effect on cross-border online transactions, while internet penetration exerts a positive and significant effect on e-commerce. The results also indicate that isolation has a positive and significant effect, suggesting that online commerce can reduce certain geographic constraints. The study deduces that African public policies should favor access to digital technology which is considered the main driver of a transformation of the African economy and cross-border logistics, while avoiding overly restrictive taxation which acts as an obstacle to development of electronic commerce.

title: From Jurisprudential Deduction to Computational Logic: A Circulation Mechanism for Industrial Vision Data Property Rights under the Separation of Three Rights
affiliations: Shanghai Polytechnic University and Shanghai Second Polytechnic University

detail.title: From Jurisprudential Deduction to Computational Logic: A Circulation Mechanism for Industrial Vision Data Property Rights under the Separation of Three Rights
detail.abstract: Data property systems are foundational for activating the value of industrial data elements. However, traditional legal contracts exhibit inherent limitations, including low execution efficiency and high enforcement costs, particularly in scenarios involving zero-cost data replication and algorithmic black boxes. Initially, a bibliometric analysis of 1,434 papers is conducted using CiteSpace, revealing a paradigm shift in data property research from static exclusion to dynamic sharing. A systemic methodology for transforming legal frameworks into executable technical architectures is lacking in current studies. To bridge this gap, a computational logic mapping model for the "Separation of Three Rights" is proposed under the "Code is Law" philosophy. This model anchors the data resource holding right using Decentralized Identifiers (DID), regulates the data processing and use right via privacy-enhancing technologies and dynamic authorization, and safeguards the data product operation right through smart contracts. To validate technical feasibility and economic effectiveness, a prototype system is constructed focusing on the visual positioning of new energy charging stations, alongside a quantitative simulation experiment involving 300 industrial nodes. Independent sample T-test results utilizing the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) demonstrate (P < 0.001) that, compared to static legal contracts, the proposed underlying computational logic can accurately quantify and significantly incentivize high-quality data supply. Furthermore, excellent end-to-end clearing and settlement latency stability is maintained under massive cross-domain, high-frequency invocations. This study provides cross-disciplinary theoretical guidance and engineering demonstrations for the compliant and efficient circulation of industrial data elements.

detail.title: Two Economies, Not One: A Taxonomy of the Agentic Economy and the Case for Settlement Neutrality

detail.abstract:
The term agentic economy appears in over fifty distinct definitions published between 2021 and March 2026 — by Microsoft Research, Sequoia Capital, the Bank for International Settlements, Coinbase, Stripe, the World Economic Forum, Gartner, Fetch.ai, and at least forty other sources. They do not mean the same thing. Some describe an AI agent buying a plane ticket for its owner through Visa. Others describe autonomous software agents negotiating, transacting, and building reputation with each other — no human in the loop, no credit card, no chargeback.

This paper surveys the definitional landscape, classifies fifty-plus usages into five categories, and identifies two fault lines that the literature has not made explicit. The first — the primary fault line — separates commerce for humans (agents as intermediaries in human economic activity) from an economy of agents (agents as independent economic actors). The second — within the autonomous category — separates the eleven approaches that require blockchain infrastructure from the one that does not.

The taxonomy reveals a structural question: what formal properties must a settlement layer possess to support autonomous agent-to-agent commerce, independent of the communication protocol and independent of the ledger substrate? We define settlement neutrality as that set of properties — escrow determinism, ledger consistency, reputation equivalence, dispute parity, and auditability — and describe a reference architecture where agents speaking Anthropic's MCP, Google's A2A, and direct REST converge on the same escrow pipeline. The paper proposes the five categories and six classification dimensions as a reusable framework for evaluating future protocols, and identifies open questions for the field.

title: Celebrating 25 Years of Progress: WIPO's Historic Advancements in Intellectual Property Rights for Local and Indigenous Communities

detail.title: Celebrating 25 Years of Progress: WIPO's Historic Advancements in Intellectual Property Rights for Local and Indigenous Communities
detail.abstract: Intellectual Property (hereinafter referred to as "IP") rights serve as a cornerstone of modern economies, incentivizing innovation, creativity, and investment. They offer creators and innovators the assurance that their efforts will be protected, encouraging them to push boundaries and contribute to societal progress. This article examines the implications of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Member States' adoption of the historic new Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources, and Associated Traditional Knowledge. The treaty establishes in international law a new disclosure requirement for patent applicants whose inventions are based on genetic resources and/or associated traditional knowledge of local or Indigenous communities. Through mapping the adoption and implementation of this treaty by various member states, this article demonstrates the diverse approaches and challenges faced in aligning national laws with international standards with further findings underscoring the importance of creating robust frameworks that not only mandate disclosure requirements, but also ensure fair and equitable benefit-sharing mechanisms to protect and empower Indigenous and local communities.

title: External Standards, Compliance Pathways, and Smallholder Exclusion: Applying the Market Suffocation Hypothesis to RSPO, EUDR, and Vietnamese Pangasius

detail.title: External Standards, Compliance Pathways, and Smallholder Exclusion: Applying the Market Suffocation Hypothesis to RSPO, EUDR, and Vietnamese Pangasius
detail.abstract:
Why does quality upgrading become systemic in some commodity systems but remain selective in others, even when the same standards and enforcement pressures apply? Existing explanations focus on premium incentives, buyer capability requirements, and regulatory design, yet these accounts fail to explain a persistent pattern: producers frequently do not upgrade despite clear incentives, while in other settings compliance becomes rapid and broad-based across the supply chain. This paper proposes that the answer lies not in the strength of the inducement but in the structure of the exit option. When producers retain access to market channels that accept non-compliant output at commercially viable prices — quality sinks — upgrading remains optional. When those channels contract sufficiently, continued non-compliance becomes commercially non-viable and upgrading becomes structurally compelled for those with viable upgrading pathways. This mechanism is formalised as the Market Suffocation Hypothesis (MSH). The framework’s comparative explanatory value lies in identifying why identical standards generate divergent distributional outcomes across contexts: it is not the standard itself but the interaction between sink closure and local upgrading pathway availability that determines whether standards transform supply chains, bifurcate them, or simply redistribute participation toward already-compliant actors.

This paper extends the MSH to externally imposed compliance standards — a class of enforcement mechanism in which market access is conditioned by standards defined outside the producing country — through three structurally distinct cases: the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) voluntary certification scheme, the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), and the transformation of Vietnam’s pangasius sector under US and EU food safety enforcement. The cases are selected to vary sink closure and upgrading pathway availability across settings, making the structural logic of the MSH visible in comparative relief. Two analytical instruments operationalise the mechanism: the Compliance Investment Threshold (CIT), which formalises the buyer’s upgrade-versus-substitute decision and generates testable predictions about smallholder inclusion; and the Compliance Viability Diagnostic (CVD), which translates CIT conditions into a prospective screening tool for resource allocation. The Suffocation Index (SI) is specified as an estimable variable with empirical proxies and a regression strategy for testing the constrained system response property formally derived in Section 1.5. The analysis is conceptual. It does not establish causal identification. It generates a structured set of predictions that are falsifiable with available panel data.

detail.abstract: Internal investigations into allegations of workplace misconduct are undertaken on a confidential basis. But confidentiality cannot be assured. Investigated employees may be revealed by the investigation, including by word of mouth and by disclosure requirements to future potential employers. Based on an experiment fielded on a large nationally representative sample, this study provides the first evidence of direct employment harm to an employee investigated for workplace misconduct or sexual harassment. Subjects express considerable opposition to a callback of applicants who were investigated for workplace misconduct, even when the investigation did not find misconduct. The findings add to the evidence documenting that any association with stigma harms employment prospects.

detail.abstract: Marketing in the metaverse is growing rapidly and so are the ethical problems that come with it. Platforms like Roblox, Meta Horizon and Decentraland collect detailed biometric and behavioral data from users as part of their marketing infrastructure, yet existing EU regulations the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), Digital Markets Act, (DMA) and Digital Service Act (DSA) were not designed with these environments in mind. This gap leaves marketers, developers and regulators unsure of how to act. We interviewed 17 experts from three groups including technology developers, marketing professionals and legal and policy specialists to understand how metaverse marketing works in practice and where current rules fall short. Our analysis directed by Gioia methodology produced four aggregate dimensions: data privacy strains in immersive marketing, transparency and ethical gaps in immersive advertising, jurisdiction and accountability deficits and the need for adaptive regulatory frameworks. Together, these dimensions indicate that consumer protection in immersive environments requires both incremental adaptation of existing laws and the co-creation of ethics-by-design practices.

title: To Fuse or Not to Fuse? Uncertainty-Aware Modality Selection for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis in E-Commerce
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) - Graduate School of Culture Technology

detail.title: To Fuse or Not to Fuse? Uncertainty-Aware Modality Selection for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis in E-Commerce
detail.abstract: Online product reviews increasingly combine text and images, fueling interest in multimodal aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA). While prior work has broadly assumed that multimodal integration universally improves performance, recent studies show it can underperform unimodal baselines under certain conditions. Focusing on the data-level properties of the review-generating context, this study proposes that uncertainty—a well-established driver of consumer behavior—is a key determinant of multimodal effectiveness in e-commerce ABSA. Drawing on market uncertainty frameworks, we extend these constructs to the individual consumer perception level, introducing Perceived Altercentric Uncertainty (PAU; consumers' uncertainty about product quality) and Consumer Perceived Egocentric Uncertainty (CPEU; consumers' inferences about producers' confidence in market success). We propose PAU/CPEU alignment as a critical condition under which multimodal fusion reliably enhances performance. Experiments conducted on a major South Korean e-commerce platform across diverse architectures and fusion strategies confirm that aligned categories yield significant multimodal gains over unimodal baselines, while misaligned categories yield smaller or negative gains. A robustness check using Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) replicates this benefit. Building on these findings, we propose a category-level, uncertainty-aware modality selection policy. Guided by PAU/CPEU alignment, this selective policy outperforms uniform always-multimodal and always-unimodal baselines, avoiding the unnecessary computational and operational overhead of indiscriminately deploying multimodal models where they provide no benefit. Ultimately, the results demonstrate that multimodal effectiveness is governed not only by algorithmic design but by the social and cognitive context in which review data is generated.

detail.abstract:
Private schools today play a significant role in delivering quality education across India. They educate millions of children to supplement the state’s role in education delivery. Presently, they operate within a legal framework that treats education as a strictly not-for-profit and charitable activity. This hampers their ability to raise investments and support day-to-day functioning. This paper 
examines constitutional philosophy, judicial precedents, and regulatory frameworks to understand how education came to be construed as not-for-profit, charitable activity even for private players. The paper also explores whether the current legal approach adequately responds to the realities of delivering quality education at scale.

detail.abstract: Right-of-way assignment at roundabouts represents one of the most fundamental divergences in international traffic management. The UK system, introduced following research by Blackmore (1963), made mandatory in 1966, requires the vehicles entering the roundabout to stop and give way to the circulating traffic, treating the roundabout as a moving stream; India follows a traditional weaving based approach as prescribed in the Indian Roads Congress code IRC:65-1976 leading to the development of various gap acceptance models to study the heterogeneous mixed traffic. In the UK, Kimber (1980) developed an empirical capacity model, following the development of the traffic priority rules. This paper presents a comparative study of these two systems with differing priority rules by implementing the aforementioned models as separate analytical queuing models in MATLAB. The UK model uses the TRRL linear capacity formula, calibrated for a typical single lane roundabout. India on the other hand employs the Modified Highway Capacity Manual(HCM) exponential formula with a multiplicative adjustment factor of 1.1, as calibrated by Mathew et al. (2017). Both the models were evaluated across arrival rates of 180 to 720 vehicles per hour per arm. Results demonstrated that the Indian model supports approximately 19% higher throughput before reaching saturation (430 vs. 360 vehicles per hour per arm). The UK model also depicted a lower average delay at moderate loads due to predictability of the traffic flow owing to the strict priority rule. These findings have implications for roundabouts design policy in nations transitioning between priority paradigms.

detail.title: Enhancing Centralized Urban Traffic Routing via Linear Programming
detail.abstract: Urbanisation growth leads to increased demands for urban road infrastructure, while exacerbating traffic congestion, especially during rush hours. This contributes to large economic losses due to delays and poses a health risk due to increased harmful emissions. Traditional traffic routing methods are typically based on decentralized strategies, which optimize routes for individual vehicles without considering the routing decisions of other vehicles. Centralized routing approaches, on the other hand, can take into account the overall traffic situation to effectively coordinate traffic flows. However, computational demands grow substantially with the increasing size of the problem.This paper proposes a new Linear Programming (LP) model that leverages the concept of multi-commodity flows for centralized traffic routing in order to effectively distribute traffic in the urban road network and mitigate the risk of traffic congestion. The introduced LP-based method is evaluated on four scenarios, two synthetic benchmarks from New York and Sydney, and two historical traffic scenarios from Dublin and Luxembourg, demonstrating better scalability and routing decisions than the state-of-the-art centralized routing methods, and outperforming the decentralized routing approach in New York and Dublin.

title: Leverage, Engagement, and Welfare in Decentralised Financial Markets
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE)

detail.title: Leverage, Engagement, and Welfare in Decentralised Financial Markets
detail.abstract: Can financial intermediaries help solve the externalities of the real-economy, even when all investors are purely return-driven? This paper develops a general equilibrium model in which firms underinvest in socially valuable transitions and investors allocate capital based solely on financial returns. In this environment, mandated activist funds that seek to influence firm behaviour are not sufficient on their own as other funds free-rides on influence outcome. However, this conclusion changes once households with limited market participation are introduced. When a subset of households saves exclusively through bank deposits, their savings provide low-cost funding that allows activist funds to access leverage through the banking system. This leverage increases the relative returns of activist funds, supports their survival in equilibrium, and enables welfare improvements. This results imply that limited stock market participation-often viewed as a friction-can play a constructive role in addressing real-economy externalities by supporting financial intermediation channels that would otherwise fail to operate.

title: The $1.50 Hot Dog is a Spence Signal, not a Loss Leader, A Tasty Teaching Note from Costco

detail.title: The $1.50 Hot Dog is a Spence Signal, not a Loss Leader, A Tasty Teaching Note from Costco

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Costco's $1.50 hot dog combo has held the same nominal price since 1985, despite cumulative inflation that would put the indexed price near $4.65. The popular and business-press explanation treats the combo as a "loss leader" in the standard supermarket sense-a below-cost item that pulls marginal foot traffic into the store. We argue this framing is simply wrong on the mechanism. Costco's rotisserie chicken arguably is a loss leader, it's a cheap and tasty meal for a family. The hot dog is not, because nobody pays $65 a year and deals with a Costco parking lot and then navigate through a 150,000-square-foot warehouse just to eat a $1.50 hot dog. The combo is a during a visit purchase by members who came for everything else. Whatever the hot dog is doing, it is not pulling traffic. The hot dog instead functions as a two-layer mechanism: a Schelling-style commitment device (Sinegal's threat to his successor raises the cost of any future price hike high enough that no successor will pay it) wrapped around a separating signal of the Spence (1973) family. We are careful about that last attribution. The signal a student first recognizes is Spence's, but the mechanism that actually does the work is the non-salvageable reputational bond of Klein and Leffler (1981): the decades-long, differentially-costly survival of the commitment-not a one-time credential-is what separates high-integrity from opportunistic firm types, a dynamic reputational structure whose modern form is the price-as-signal literature (Aleksenko and Kohlhepp 2025). A toy two-equation model, calibrated to Costco's FY2025 10-K, makes the asymmetry quantitative: a 50¢ hike would collect at most $75M in incremental margin, against roughly $6.85B of US operating income that depends on the trust the anchor secures. A formal proposition follows: the trust function has a discrete drop at the commitment anchor, so any positive hike pays the entire bond-destruction cost and collects only the marginal subsidy savings; the model admits no interior optimum above $1.50. As a teaching extension-outside the strict scope of the proposition-we describe a rule-bound replacement bond (an inflation-indexed, rounded-down-by-rule price announced years before its first invocation) that could in principle preserve credibility while permitting price evolution, conditional on flawless multi-year execution. The note is written for use as a teaching example connecting classical signaling and commitment theory to a familiar, publicly observable case.

detail.abstract: Purpose - This study examines how different types of constraints influence delay outcomes in utility-scale solar farm civil construction and proposes a constraint-based taxonomy comprising Physical, Socio-environmental and Technical-operational categories. It also introduces Earthwork Volume Intensity (EVI, m³/MWp) as a terrain-normalised indicator of earthwork demand. Design/methodology/approach - A multiple-case study design is applied to eight solar farm projects in Thailand (169 MWp total) delivered under standardised equipment and contractual conditions. Primary schedule data are analysed through cross-case pattern analysis and exploratory statistical methods, including Pearson correlation, ordinary least squares regression and the MannWhitney U test. Findings - Within hillside terrain, EVI provides a more consistent explanation of delay severity than project scale, indicating a direct link between terrain-driven workload and schedule performance. Hillside projects experienced substantially higher earthwork delays (36- 57%) than flat-terrain projects, while foundation delays were effectively mitigated through a change in construction method (driven concrete to steel screw piles). The apparent correlation between project scale and delay reflects outlier leverage rather than a causal mechanism. Research limitations/implications - The sample size (n = 8) and single-organisation data source limit statistical power and generalisability. EVI is positioned as a planning-oriented diagnostic rather than a statistically validated predictor; validation across larger, multi-organisation datasets is required. Practical implications - The constraint taxonomy and EVI metric provide a structured pre-construction decision framework supporting differentiated contingency allocation by terrain type, agricultural-calendar coordination for socio-environmental risks and geotechnical-informed foundation selection. Owner’s Engineers managing multi-site portfolios can apply the framework using routinely collected schedule data. Originality/value - This is the first study to apply a constraint-based delay taxonomy to solar farm civil construction and to introduce EVI as a terrainderived schedule risk indicator. The single-organisation controlled design isolates terrain effects from confounders typically present in multi-organisation construction delay studies.

title: Rule-of-Law Backsliding, Sustainability Rollback, and International Business in the Trump Era

detail.abstract:
Purpose of this paper: This viewpoint paper examines how the return of the Trump administration is reshaping international business, sustainability governance and global institutions. Organised as a structured bricolage of three interrelated viewpoints, it analyses how rule-of-law backsliding, sustainability rollback and business-and-human-rights reconfiguration challenge responsible business and sustainable development frameworks.
Originality/value: The paper contributes to international business scholarship by linking geopolitical shifts, regulatory change, corporate strategy, neoliberal political economy and business-and-human-rights governance. It shows that the Trump II era is not merely a period of policy reversal or heightened political risk, but a deeper destabilisation of the legal, institutional and normative conditions on which responsible international business depends. - Design/methodology/approach: The paper adopts a conceptual and qualitative approach, combining policy and document analysis with critical perspectives from international business, international political economy and political science. It synthesises three viewpoints on EU sustainability rollback, neoliberal capitalism and the politicisation of business and human rights. - Findings: Recent political shifts contribute to the rollback and contestation of sustainability and human-rights governance. Across the three viewpoints, rollback through politicisation emerges as a common mechanism: sustainability regulation, ESG, DEI, due diligence and human rights are weakened by being reframed as anti-competitive, ideological, sovereignty-threatening or hostile to national economic interests. - Research limitations/implications: Future research should examine how firms, states, business associations and civil society actors weaken, contest or defend sustainability and human-rights governance, including beyond the US–EU axis. - Practical implications: Managers and policymakers need resilient governance, due-diligence and political-risk systems for fragmented sustainability and human-rights regimes. - Social implications: Rollback may weaken climate, labour-rights and social-equity efforts, with consequences for suppliers, workers and communities embedded in global value chains.

detail.abstract: The pharmaceutical supply chain suffers from a persistent and costly inefficiency: critical batch data generated digitally by Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations (CDMOs) is transmitted to drug product manufacturers as static PDF certificates or Excel spreadsheets, forcing skilled personnel to manually re-enter data into Quality Management Systems (QMS). This introduces transcription errors, delays batch release, undermines data integrity, and creates compliance risk under Good Practice (GxP) regulations. This paper presents a Design Science Research (DSR) artefactthe AAS Open Exchange Portalan interactive platform demonstrating how the Asset Administration Shell (AAS) standard, developed by the Industrial Digital Twin Association (IDTA), can eliminate this bottleneck through automated, machineto-machine batch data exchange between CDMOs and brand owners. The artefact was initially developed during the ISPE Emerging Leader Hackathon (April 2026, Copenhagen), sponsored by Roche, and subsequently extended into a universal MVP. The platform demonstrates bidirectional data exchange, Digital Calibration Certificate (DCC) integration, role-based access control using Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC), AI-driven demand forecasting, a GxP-compliant audit trail, and a manual bridge mode for organisations not yet fully integrated. The AAS exchange is implemented as a browser-based simulation using client-side JavaScript; no live AAS server or production API was deployed, consistent with the scope of a DSR feasibility study. The paper evaluates the artefact against ALCOA+ data integrity principles, EU GMP Annex 11 requirements, and WHO traceability mandates, demonstrating that the AAS standard is not only technically feasible for pharmaceutical supply chain data exchange but natively satisfies regulatory requirements that current PDF-based workflows actively violate.

title: China Green Tech and its Industrial Policy
affiliations: Bruegel

detail.title: China Green Tech and its Industrial Policy
detail.abstract: This paper examines China’s emergence as the dominant global manufacturer of green technology, a development originally driven by its pressing domestic need to address environmental degradation and energy security. By implementing a comprehensive industrial strategy anchored in the strategic acquisition of foreign technology, extensive state subsidization, and the cultivation of a hypercompetitive domestic market, China has achieved unparalleled production capacity. Consequently, this capacity now significantly outstrips global demand, transforming China into the primary green technology supplier for the world. While this dynamic exports deflationary pressures that make global decarbonization more affordable, it simultaneously presents a formidable competitive challenge to foreign industries. The paper concludes by exploring strategic pathways for developing nations. It argues that the Global South must form robust regional alliances to aggregate market demand, leverage critical mineral resources, and build complementary manufacturing capabilities to successfully navigate this new, China-centric industrial landscape.

title: When Decentralization Stops Working: A Framework for AI Governance under Changing Risk Structures

detail.title: When Decentralization Stops Working: A Framework for AI Governance under Changing Risk Structures
detail.abstract:
Debates over AI governance frequently assume that decentralized, adaptive approaches and centralized regulatory oversight are competing alternatives. This article argues that the choice between them depends on the structure of risk, not prior assumptions about government or markets. I propose a diagnostic framework organized around two dimensions: asymmetry (the balance of potential upside to downside) and boundedness (whether harms remain containable or cascade systemically). Together these dimensions reveal when decentralized adaptation remains reliable and when it breaks down.


As systems scale, couple, accelerate, or generate deep uncertainty, both dimensions shift: risks become less bounded and increasingly negatively asymmetric. These structural changes erode the conditions that make decentralized correction effective — localized feedback, reversibility, observability, and bounded exposure — and require governance responses to shift accordingly. The article introduces a framework of graduated governance that matches institutional responses to underlying risk structure: decentralized mechanisms where risks remain bounded and positively asymmetric; coordinated risk management where harms propagate or incentives externalize systemic risk; and precautionary constraint coordination (i.e., management under feedback collapse) where deep uncertainty and irreversibility make iterative correction unreliable.


The framework offers scholars a diagnostic vocabulary for classifying AI risks by their structural properties and contributes to debates on regulatory delegation, risk governance, and institutional design under uncertainty. For policymakers, it provides a practical basis for determining when systems have crossed the threshold where decentralized correction can no longer be trusted.

title: Tackling India's Jobs Plight: Underutilised Levers and Lessons from China
affiliations: Bruegel and Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research (IGIDR)

detail.title: Tackling India's Jobs Plight: Underutilised Levers and Lessons from China
detail.abstract: Despite strong GDP growth and a favourable demographic profile, India faces an impending jobs crisis. A large share of the workforce remains employed in lowproductivity agriculture, while many new labour market entrants are absorbed into the persistently large informal sector. By contrast, China's rapid ascent was driven by manufacturing-led, export-oriented industrialisation, underpinned by large inflows of foreign direct investment and sustained technology transfer. India's manufacturing base remains modest in contrast. The bulk of well-paid, formal employment continues to be concentrated in the high-skill services sector. This paper contrasts the development trajectories of these two economies and identifies several underutilised jobs-growth levers in India: manufacturing, goods exports, manufacturing-oriented foreign direct investment and innovation. All of these remain underdeveloped, yet together they offer a pathway to more labour-absorbing, durable growth. Leveraging them effectively would be central to achieving India's 'Viksit Bharat 2047' ambition of attaining high-income status. The scale of India's challenge to employ eight to ten million labour-market entrants per year implies that job creation must become an explicit policy priority. This calls for greater trade openness, particularly with Asia and Europe, to integrate India into Asia-centric global supply chains as an alternative to China. Labour market reform is equally critical, making the effective implementation of the new labour codes essential. Strengthening innovation ecosystems and realigning education and skills policies to support industrialisation are also key. Without these structural shifts, India's current pattern of jobless growth risks transforming its demographic dividend into a long-term liability.

A Theory of Tacit Fusion

detail.title:
The Silent Drift of Forensic Accounting Expert Testimony from Objectivity to Advocacy:
A Theory of Tacit Fusion
detail.abstract: Previous forensic accounting research on expert witnessing has identified expert bias as an ethical failure and has harshly criticized the profession, presuming that biased testimony reflects a conscious decision. This paper challenges that view by introducing Tacit Fusion Theory, an unconscious framework that explains the silent expert drift toward the party that compensates them as they adapt to the adversarial system. Integrating discretion points with Social Identity Theory, the paper proposes that the drift develops through a three-stage recurrent process: 1) discretion point ambiguity, 2) "in-group" identification with the legal team, and 3) the silent drift. The process is illustrated by categorizing discretion points that allow for subjectivity, thereby creating subconscious alignment. The outcome implies that the current setting is not equipped to mitigate expert fusion and that the process should be treated as a structural conflict rather than an individual matter.

title: Volatility Drag and the Perpetual Borrowing Option: The Admissible Financing Boundary

detail.title: Volatility Drag and the Perpetual Borrowing Option: The Admissible Financing Boundary

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Thomas J. The paper was prepared independently, and the analysis, conclusions, and opinions expressed are solely those of the author.

detail.abstract:
Modern Portfolio Theory specifies optimal portfolio composition but is largely silent on financing policy through time. That silence has a calculable cost. Under geometric Brownian motion, a risky portfolio compounds at its arithmetic return less one-half its variance. The resulting drag, equal to one-half variance per year, is exact under the model, independent of expected return, and unavoidable within an unfinanced buy-and-hold path. This paper designates that cost and asks whether it is recoverable.

The paper models unused borrowing capacity as a perpetual American-style financing option and applies McKean’s optimal-exercise framework. Under continuous gross-exposure pinning to the arithmetic benchmark, the equity-to-benchmark ratio follows an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck recovery process that mean-reverts toward full recovery. The recovered quantity is designated . The same dynamics that produce recovery also assign positive probability to ruin; over an infinite horizon, ruin becomes unavoidable under the unconstrained policy. An admissibility constraint is therefore not an auxiliary assumption but a mathematical necessity. The constrained financing region defined by that requirement is .

The admissible region is characterized by seven points, A through G, spanning no financing through certain ruin. The dominant variable is time: over horizons of 15 to 50 years, an admissible financing policy is shown to recover Itô’s Zeta in expectation. Empirical demonstration across 5,000,000 simulated paths and 100 independent seeds shows full recovery, with McKean’s Alpha approximately equal to Itô’s Zeta, at volatility of 15 percent or below across all borrowing rates tested, with near-zero ruin probability. Long-horizon bootstrap analysis using 10,000 resamplings yields a 95 percent confidence interval for the McKean’s Alpha to Itô’s Zeta ratio of 1.0000 to 1.0004. The simulation evidence supports the conjecture that Itô’s Zeta equals McKean’s Alpha and equals one-half variance exactly, although the analytical proof remains open.

The framework is distinguished from Merton and Kelly by sequence. Merton and Kelly are first-mover rules that optimize in anticipation of volatility drag. Spiral Theory is a second-mover rule that responds after deviation from the arithmetic benchmark is observed. Portfolio construction and financing policy are therefore distinct, separately solvable problems. The paper proposes that Itô’s Zeta and McKean’s Alpha be reported explicitly alongside expected arithmetic return in investment policy statements, financial plans, and performance reports.

title: The IPO Gender Gap
affiliations: , Brigham Young University - J. Reuben Clark Law School and

detail.title: The IPO Gender Gap
detail.abstract:
Elite transactional practice drives record-breaking profits for lawyers at top-tier law firms. Lawyers at transactional powerhouses not only stand to gain financially; they also wield significant influence over the broader economy and society. Yet, power dynamics within these firms remain largely unexamined. Over the last two decades, the proportion of women partners in law firms has risen, albeit slowly. Despite some progress, there is a dearth of research focused on specific practice areas that could reveal whether women have achieved substantial gains in the most lucrative practice areas, or if they have secured central roles within the network of lawyers specializing in those fields.

Within the subset of transactional practice, capital markets practice is an especially important and networked system. And the crème de la crème of capital markets practice is advising companies and underwriters in initial public offerings (IPOs). Lawyers representing companies and underwriters are frequently repeat players who gain substantial financial rewards and deep expertise from working on these high-profile transactions. Given the significant public visibility of IPOs, firms and lawyers often build their reputations and brands by being seen as the go-to lawyers for IPOs. IPO practice is particularly fruitful as the lawyers advising on an IPO typically proceed to advise the company on the regulatory and corporate governance complexity of being a publicly traded company. Moreover, firms and lawyers known for advising underwriters in IPOs are turned to repeatedly for advisory engagements by elite investment banks.

This Article presents the first empirical study of the gender gap within the network of lawyers leading IPO advisory work (the “IPO Attorney Network”). Analyzing thousands of lawyers across 8,358 IPOs over a 22-year period, our findings highlight persistent systemic exclusion of women. First, we uncover a dramatically persistent gender gap in the IPO Attorney Network. Our study shows that the gender gap among lawyers advising on IPOs was virtually unchanged between 2000 and 2021—that is a 22-year period with dramatic stagnation. We find a similar pattern when we examine attorneys’ network centrality: over time, far more men become highly connected lawyers in the network than women. Importantly, we find evidence that women in the IPO Advisory Network have inferior access to network resources—e.g., more connections to high degree individuals in the network—than men as their careers progress, suggesting the existence of persistent professional obstacles to career success and advancement. Second, we find that the gender gap differs by the type of IPO. For IPOs of Special Purpose Acquisition Companies (SPACs)—IPOs that have come under heavy criticism by both academics and investors—the gender gap is even greater. Third, we find material differences in gender representation between law firms advising the IPO market. Our study shows that the gender gap is especially pronounced at some of the most elite law firms advising on IPOs. Fourth, we find evidence that the gender gap is larger when lawyers represent underwriters—that is the elite investment banks that themselves are known for experiencing significant gender disparities. Fifth, we find no evidence of correlation between the incidence of women general counsel in an IPO and gender representation among advisory teams. Sixth, we find that geographic location matters in evaluating the gender gap, and that when representing issuers the gender gap is greater for attorneys practicing in New York than those practicing in California.

Amidst growing attacks on diversity and inclusion initiatives across various institutions, including law firms, our findings serve as a crucial warning. First, they raise doubts about the impact of decades-long diversity and inclusion practices at law firms on lowering the gender gap in transactional practice. Second, considering the slow pace of progress over almost two decades, our research suggests that abandoning all diversity and inclusion efforts could exacerbate the gender gap in transactional practice. In a profession that prides itself on fairness and equality, the current debate over law firms’ diversity practices offers a timely opportunity for leaders to develop strategies that genuinely advance opportunities for all lawyers.

title: The Role of Working Capital Management Practices in Fostering Entrepreneurial Performance among Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)

detail.title: The Role of Working Capital Management Practices in Fostering Entrepreneurial Performance among Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)
detail.abstract: In today's competitive business environment, entrepreneurial performance has become a critical indicator of how effectively small and medium enterprises (SMEs) sustain their operations and achieve business success. One important factor that can influence this performance is the way entrepreneurs manage their financial resources, particularly through effective working capital management practices. This study examined the role of working capital management practices in fostering the perceived entrepreneurial performance of SMEs in Carmen, Cagayan de Oro City, Philippines. The study employed a descriptive-correlational research design. Data were collected from 102 SME owners and managers using an adapted and validated survey questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Mann-Whitney test, the Kruskal-Wallis test, and linear regression analysis. The results affirm that working capital management practices were described as very good, highlighting effective handling of short-term financial resources necessary for daily operations. The perceived entrepreneurial performance was likewise assessed at a very high level, reflecting positive business outputs and outcomes. No significant differences were observed in working capital management practices and perceived entrepreneurial performance when respondents were grouped according to their organizational profile. However, regression analysis confirmed that among the components of working capital management practices, only inventory management and cash management had a statistically significant influence on perceived entrepreneurial performance, with inventory management exerting the strongest influence, followed by cash management. This finding highlights the vital role of effective working capital management practices in sustaining the entrepreneurial performance of small and medium enterprises. By strengthening financial resource management, SMEs are better positioned to maintain operational efficiency, support business stability, and achieve long-term business success in a competitive environment.

detail.title: Enhancing community-based One Health surveillance: Insights from the ALERT game-based case study in Cameroon
detail.abstract: Zoonotic diseases have significant implications for public health. Increasing knowledge and stakeholder engagement is therefore essential to ensure their early detection. This study assessed the short-term effects of the ALERT serious game on stakeholders involved in disease surveillance in Cameroon. ALERT is a collaborative serious board game focusing on best practices in surveillance, based on the One Health approach. This study was conducted in the Campo district in southern Cameroon. It involved subprefectural technical staff from various sectors (livestock, public health and wildlife), as well as staff members from the Campo subprefecture and community stakeholders. The general evaluation framework used here is based on the New World Kirkpatrick Model, a conceptual framework commonly used to evaluate training programs that is also suitable for assessing the effects of games. Participants’ reactions during and after the game and the degree of learning were evaluated, with data collected using participatory and qualitative methods. Based on the two criteria assessed, the evaluation indicated participant satisfaction with the game while also highlighting several limitations. It also demonstrated that participants enhanced their understanding of zoonotic diseases and the associated surveillance challenges after playing the game. Additionally, participants showed a stronger appreciation for cross-sector collaboration and identified specific actions to strengthen such collaboration at the district level. New stakeholders were identified and integrated into the proposed community-based surveillance system and the criteria for evaluating its effective operation. These findings underscore the need to evaluate post-game actions and to co-construct support to ensure their effective translation into practice.

detail.abstract: Procurement often relies on bilateral negotiations that are susceptible to information asymmetry and sub-optimal price discovery. This paper explores the transition to a mechanism-based negotiation, leveraging applied game theory to establish rules that drive supplier competition for contract awards and thereby deliver cost savings to the buyer. Centered on the 3Cs, Competition, Comparability, and Credibility, the study evaluates various auction formats, including English, Dutch, and hybrid "Anglo-Dutch" designs. The paper demonstrates how real-world factors such as risk aversion and capacity constraints favor specific mechanisms. Furthermore, it introduces a quantitative framework for lot sizing to balance economies of scale with market competitiveness. To ensure "apples-to-apples" evaluations, the authors advocate for the Comparison Price Approach, monetizing qualitative differences into transparent adjustments. By transforming the buyer’s role from seller adversary to market referee, the likelihood of low-cost and high-quality outcomes increases.

keywords: Quantifying Retail Inventory Loss: A Combined Shrinkage and Stockout Analytics Framework for Distribution Centers

detail.abstract: Inventory stockouts represent a persistent operational challenge in retail distribution, with prior work estimating losses between 4% and 8% of potential revenue (Gruen, Corsten & Bharadwaj, 2002). A companion study (Okorji, 2026) quantified $163.9M in stockout losses across five simulated distribution centers over twelve months. The present study extends this descriptive framework into a prescriptive and predictive system by developing reorder point optimization and machine learning demand forecasting models designed to prevent identified losses. Three forecasting models are evaluated using a holdout validation approach: Linear Regression as baseline, Random Forest with feature engineering, and Prophet (formerly Facebook Prophet) for time series decomposition. Models are trained on 336 days of daily transaction data per SKU-warehouse combination and evaluated on a 30-day holdout test set across 500 SKU-warehouse combinations spanning five distribution centers and 100 product SKUs. Results demonstrate that Random Forest achieves the lowest Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE = 11.54 units) representing a 48.4% improvement over the Linear Regression baseline (RMSE = 22.37). Prophet achieves RMSE = 16.65 with the additional benefit of uncertainty quantification through confidence intervals. Feature importance analysis identifies monthly seasonality and 7-day rolling demand as the strongest predictors, consistent with Q4 holiday demand patterns identified in the companion study. The reorder point framework, incorporating safety stock at a 95% service level (Z = 1.65) and a 7-day assumed lead time, identifies 364 of 500 SKU-warehouse combinations (72.8%) at critical stockout risk. Scenario analysis estimates between $114.7M (conservative, 70% prevention) and $147.5M (aggressive, 90% prevention) in recoverable losses through optimization implementation. Savings estimates are simulation-based projections. Results are based on a synthetic retail simulation environment with fixed lead time assumptions and should be interpreted as modeled estimates requiring empirical validation in production settings. The complete pipeline is publicly available for replication at https://github.com/Kani35000/predictive-inventory-pipeline.

detail.abstract:
Without fanfare, U.S. companies, financiers, and entrepreneurs are continuing to make substantial investments in reducing emissions of carbon, methane, and other greenhouse gases (GHGs) and, in a growing trend, in direct removals of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. In April 2025, for example, the X Prize Carbon Removal competition doled out $100 million in the largest global incentive competition award in history.

While many clean energy investments will continue to scale, a single market failure—the lack of investor-grade performance metrics—threatens to hold back investments in three of the most promising opportunity areas for GHG emissions reductions and removals: methane emissions reductions; hybrid (or engineered) CDR solutions; and forest carbon interventions.

The Stanford Law & Policy Lab report describes how poor performance accounting standards are the soft underbelly that is afflicting each of these sectors. In all three cases, there is no general agreement on protocols that should be used to measure and confirm GHG reductions and removals, nor is there a system for transparently sharing performance results that will trigger additional investment.

This lack of GHG performance accounting can and must be fixed. The Stanford report reviews how leaders in other fields have come together to identify and incentivize the use of modern data management tools to pool together shared, trusted performance information that data users of all types can rely upon. The report provides recommendations for how key stakeholders in each of the three sectors highlighted in the report can—with the assistance of expert convenors and university consortia—leverage and expand nascent standard-setting and data collection and sharing initiatives to generate accessible, trusted GHG performance data, triggering increased investment in activities that will reduce methane emissions, scale CDR solutions, and increase carbon uptake in forests (and other nature-based solutions). The report also highlights GHG performance data gains that can be made in the urban context, building on foundational work undertaken by Crosswalk Labs and the Data Foundation.

detail.abstract: Cancer remains a leading global health challenge, with conventional diagnostic and treatment methods often lacking precision and adaptability. This comprehensive review explores transformative advancements that are reshaping oncology, emphasizing the integration of biomarker-driven diagnostics with tailored therapeutic strategies. It examines the complex etiology of neoplastic disease, the systemic patient experience, and evolving surgical paradigms ranging from minimally invasive robotics to complex cytoreductive procedures. Additionally, it highlights the critical role of artificial intelligence as a supportive, evidence-organizing co-pilot within multidisciplinary tumor boards. Furthermore, the review outlines the far-reaching consequences of cancer for health systems, economies, and societies, highlighting the urgent need to address equitable access to life-saving technologies and care worldwide. 1 By adopting cutting-edge, patient-centered approaches, a new era of precision oncology emerges, bridging the gap between early detection and effective intervention.

title: Predictive Maintenance Beyond the Hype: Total Cost of Ownership Models for Industrial AI Deployments

detail.title: Predictive Maintenance Beyond the Hype: Total Cost of Ownership Models for Industrial AI Deployments
detail.abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) is the most frequently cited use case for Industrial AI, featured prominently in vendor marketing, industry conference agendas, and enterprise AI strategy documents. Yet the actual return on investment for predictive maintenance AI remains poorly understood, obscured by vendor-driven narratives that emphasize sensor cost reductions and downtime avoidance while systematically underreporting the true costs of deployment. This paper argues that the total cost of ownership for predictive maintenance AI is 2.5-4x higher than vendor projections typically suggest, and that the breakeven horizon is correspondingly longer than most capital expenditure approvals anticipate. Drawing on transaction cost economics and evidence from discrete manufacturing and process industry deployments, the paper proposes the PdM-TCO Framework-a five-stage total cost of ownership model specifically designed for predictive maintenance AI that captures costs across instrumentation, data pipeline construction, model development, operational integration, and continuous improvement. The framework identifies five categories of systematically underreported costs: data engineering infrastructure, change management for maintenance teams, false positive fatigue and its trust erosion effects, model retraining as equipment degrades, and organizational integration overhead. The paper further proposes the PdM Investment Justification Matrix, which identifies the conditions-asset criticality, failure consequence severity, data availability, and maintenance team readiness-under which predictive maintenance AI investment is genuinely justified versus conditions under which simpler condition-based monitoring delivers equivalent value at lower cost. Implications are developed for VP Operations evaluating PdM investments, Plant Managers implementing PdM programs, and CFOs approving capital expenditure for Industrial AI.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how regulatory thresholds a ect the pricing and structure of small business lending. I exploit the 10 billion Dollar asset cuto in the Dodd-Frank Act, which imposes enhanced regulatory requirements on banks, to isolate the impact of regulation on lending outcomes. Banks crossing the threshold increase loan spreads and adjust contract terms by reducing loan size, shortening maturity, and increasing reliance on government guarantees after the implementation of Dodd-Frank act. detail.abstract: Climate policy often assumes that renewable energy deployment produces similar emission reductions across countries, despite major differences in grid flexibility and fuel substitution capacity. Using the GTAP-E-Power computable general equilibrium framework calibrated to eight global regions and twenty-two sectors, together with panel data for 59 countries from 2000 to 2023, this paper examines how technology-specific renewable shocks affect emissions, production, and welfare. The results reveal a heterogeneous rebound problem in which developing economies with rigid grids experience emissions declines of 16-33% through output contraction, while advanced economies substitute toward fossil generation, producing rebound effects of up to 39% under solar shocks. Solar shocks generate the strongest rebounds, while firm zero-emission baseload contractions intensify coal substitution. Demand-side efficiency policies generate substantial welfare gains but impose negative spillovers on trade-exposed regions. Fixed-effects and Bayesian Ridge methods consistently confirm a robust emissions-reducing effect of renewable energy deployment, with a fixed-effects elasticity of-0.30 and a Bayesian Ridge posterior mean of-0.40.

detail.title: Twenty Years After a Turning Point: Legacies, Lessons, and the Unfinished Business of Institutional Denial and Heads and Hearts
detail.abstract:
This article examines the lasting impact of two landmark articles that transformed modern legal education: Lawrence Krieger’s Institutional Denial About the Dark Side of Law School and Gerald Hess’s Heads and Hearts: The Teaching and Learning Environment in Law School. Together, the articles identified how law school structures, culture, and teaching practices contribute to student distress, alienation, loss of intrinsic motivation, and weakened professional identity, while also offering concrete approaches for creating more humane and effective learning environments.

The article traces how these works reshaped legal education over the last two decades, influencing scholarship, teaching practices, faculty development, well-being initiatives, and ABA accreditation standards related to professional identity and student wellness. It also argues, however, that much of the core problem remains unresolved. Despite widespread reform efforts, many of the structural conditions the authors criticized, especially mandatory grading curves and competitive institutional cultures, continue to define legal education.

Twenty years later, the unfinished business of these articles remains clear: legal education cannot meaningfully improve student well-being, learning, or professional formation without confronting both the systems that govern law schools and the daily teaching practices that shape students’ experiences.

title: Beyond the Single Binary Choice Format for Eliciting Willingness to Accept: Evidence from a Field Study on Onshore Wind Farms

detail.title: Beyond the Single Binary Choice Format for Eliciting Willingness to Accept: Evidence from a Field Study on Onshore Wind Farms
detail.abstract: This study examines the convergent validity of alternative elicitation formats for estimating willingness to accept (WTA) in the field, using a single binary choice (SBC) question as the benchmark. We consider standard and theory-driven versions (based on mechanism-design theory) of the double-bounded binary choice (DB) and the open-ended (OE) formats. Our empirical application, conducted in collaboration with a major energy company, elicits the compensation required for installing onshore wind farms in respondents' municipalities. To account for the high compensation amounts, we use a novel econometric approach that accommodates nonlinear utility of compensation for binary choice formats. We find strong evidence against convergent validity for both versions of the OE format. The DB format, especially in the theory-driven version, yields WTA estimates comparable in magnitude to those obtained in the SBC, both on average and when accounting for heterogeneity in preferences. These findings indicate that the OE format is not suitable for WTA elicitation, while a well-designed DB can yield WTA estimates comparable to those obtained using the SBC format.

detail.abstract: This study explores the traditional occupational titles among the Hausa people to uncover the deep thoughts and philosophies reflected in their cultural expressions, especially through proverbs. Proverbs serve as a key to understanding how the Hausa view authority, leadership, and the value of work within their traditional crafts and professions. The research is guided by Max Weber's (1922) Theory of Authority, which helps explain how power and respect are structured in these traditional roles. The study has two main goals: first, to collect proverbs tied to certain occupational titles, and second, to interpret the wisdom and philosophical ideas behind them. It also seeks to answer two major questions: (i) What kinds of proverbs are found in these traditional occupational titles? (ii) What philosophical insights or cultural meanings do these proverbs carry? Four traditional titles were selected for analysis: Sarkin Ɗori (Chief Bone Setters), Sarkin Fawa (Chief Butchers), Sarkin Gini (Chief Builders), and Sarkin Ƙira (Chief Blacksmiths). The findings reveal that each of these titles is enriched with proverbs that express the Hausa people's values, intelligence, and understanding of authority, labor, and tradition.

Italian Abstract: Il termine open banking si riferisce alla possibilità che terze parti accedano a dati e informazioni relativi ai conti correnti tenuti presso le banche dai clienti, con l’assenso di questi ultimi, al fine di fornire loro nuovi servizi e applicazioni. Il lavoro illustra le caratteristiche dell’open banking, il suo impatto sul mercato italiano dei pagamenti e le conseguenti modifiche nelle procedure di vigilanza e sorveglianza che regolano le relazioni dell’autorità finanziaria con i nuovi attori della catena dei pagamenti e assicurano il mantenimento nel tempo dell’equilibrio complessivo del sistema. Nel mercato italiano, a seguito dell’applicazione della normativa comunitaria stabilita nella Direttiva PSD2, le interfacce predisposte dai prestatori di servizi di pagamento per consentire l’accesso di terze parti fanno prevalentemente leva su soluzioni di sistema, infrastrutture tecniche che realizzano un unico punto di accesso per una pluralità di intermediari. L’Autorità nazionale competente, nelle sue funzioni di vigilanza e supervisione, ha sviluppato inoltre un sistema dei controlli che tengono conto delle nuove caratteristiche del mercato, fortemente innovative. L’attività di sorveglianza prevede inoltre la raccolta di dati statistici per il monitoraggio dei profili di efficienza, affidabilità, sicurezza e conformità delle soluzioni di sistema, consentendo l’elaborazione di indicatori utili per valutare l’evoluzione del mercato nazionale.
English Abstract: This paper describes the features of open banking, its impact on the Italian payments market, and the changes it has brought about in the supervisory and oversight procedures of Banca d'Italia, the competent financial authority, implemented to govern relations with the new players in the payment chain and to ensure that the overall stability of the payment system is maintained over time. In the Italian market, the application of EU regulations, set out in PSD2, led to the development of system solutions, based on hubs, to which payment service providers turned to a great extent to set up dedicated interfaces for third-party access. The national competent authority, in its supervisory and oversight functions, has set out system of controls, provided for by the regulations, to respond to the new and highly innovative characteristics of the market. The oversight activity also includes the collection of statistical data to monitor the efficiency, reliability, security and compliance profiles of the system solutions, enabling the development of useful indicators to assess the evolution of the national market.

title: ADR as a Pillar for Sustainable Electoral Governance and Peace in Africa
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: ADR as a Pillar for Sustainable Electoral Governance and Peace in Africa
detail.abstract: Electoral disputes in Africa transcend mere legal technicalities to encompass complex political, social, and psychological dynamics. While litigation upholds legal mandates, it operates within a rigid, adversarial framework that often fails to address the deep-seated relational and societal repercussions of contested polls. Regional and continental dispute resolution frameworks that integrate Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) provide essential avenues for dialogue, reconciliation, and conflict prevention that are both culturally grounded and politically sustainable. Drawing on extensive experience in electoral governance, mediation, psychological counseling, and peace advocacy, this paper argues that ADR-when formally institutionalized within both regional and domestic systems-can significantly enhance democratic consolidation and peace in Africa. By examining the roles of the African Union (AU), sub-regional bodies, and domestic electoral management institutions, this paper concludes that ADR is no longer a mere "alternative" but a governance imperative for the 21st-century African polity.
