Overall, the findings show that Italian schools can increase their output by around 15% (private) or 20% (public), using the same available resources. Private schools are more efficient than their public counterparts, and they are also more productive in developing SESs.

detail.abstract: As the supply network for community-based elderly care services expands, the research focus shifts from mere service availability to computationally modeling who can access and utilize services effectively. Existing studies often consider accessibility as spatial distance or economic cost and equity as simple resource allocation, limiting insights into cumulative disadvantages faced by older adults with low income, digital barriers, or limited family support. Based on data from 3,800 community elder care sites across 20 U.S. metropolitan areas, individual survey data from 6,240 older adults, and community socioeconomic indicators, this study constructs a computational five-stage accessibility chain model: "Information Accessibility-Eligibility Determination-Process Accessibility-Service Availability-Outcome Attainability."The study integrates heterogeneous data encoding, adaptive spatial accessibility computation, stage-aware vulnerability representation, and hierarchical modeling. Two-Step Floating Contour Analysis (2SFCA), stage-coupled logit modeling, and deep embedded clustering are applied to stratify risk and optimize service access prediction. A cross-vulnerability index, combining six factors-age, income, cognition, language proficiency, family support, and digital access-is incorporated into the model to quantify cumulative impacts across stages.Preliminary results indicate that inequalities do not primarily arise from geographic proximity but accumulate during intermediate phases of information identification, eligibility determination, and process navigation. Digital vulnerability and lack of family support remain major limiting factors even after controlling for spatial accessibility, demonstrating the effectiveness of stage-aware, computationally optimized modeling. This paper proposes an integrated "accessibility chain-intersectional vulnerability" computational framework, advancing service equity from outcome equity to process and transformational equity, and providing a technology-driven foundation for targeted service allocation, navigation system optimization, and identification of high-risk groups in community-based elderly care.

title: Employment Effects of the Inflation Reduction Act

detail.abstract: One of the key justifications for the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) was its potential to create jobs. I examine the short-run employment effects of the IRA's clean electricity tax credits using industry-by-county data from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages. I implement a synthetic difference-indifferences design, comparing counties with high propensity for solar and battery development to those without, based on irradiance and transmission capacity. By 2025Q2, employment increased by nearly 100 jobs per county in directly-related construction industries (an 18% increase relative to the pre-IRA mean), with spillovers of approximately 90 jobs per county in related construction industries (a 17% increase). These gains amount to an increase of 190,000 jobs, or 2.2 jobs per MW of new solar and battery storage capacity. Local gains were concentrated in populous counties whose residents were more likely to support climate policy, limiting the scope for the law's tax credits to build new political constituencies.

detail.abstract: This public working paper develops a conceptual and quantitative framework for transforming a portion of African public debt into productive concessionary assets through an instrument called the African Debt-for-Development Concession, abbreviated as ADDC. The paper starts from a historical problem: public debt has expanded globally and in Africa, but many borrowing cycles have not produced a sufficient stock of self-liquidating productive assets. Conventional restructuring, refinancing and relief can reduce liquidity pressure, yet they do not automatically create ports, logistics corridors, energy platforms, industrial zones, digital infrastructure or export capacity. ADDC therefore reframes part of the debt question as a conversion problem: under what conditions can a sovereign claim be reorganised into economic rights linked to a governed productive asset? The paper integrates debt-for-development swaps, sovereign recovery analysis, public-private partnerships, concession governance, special economic zones and institutional economics. Its main contribution is a dual-sided public model: a debtor eligibility logic, a creditor attractiveness logic and a joint viability rule. The public version keeps the equations general and the stress tests stylised. It is intended as an academic screening framework, not as a complete transaction manual.

detail.title: Macroeconomic Determinants of Corruption: An Empirical Analysis of Eastern European Countries
detail.abstract: Corruption is a complex issue that undermines institutional integrity, distorts economic incentives and significantly contributes to disparities in economic development and inequality. The phenomenon is influenced by a range of factors and we examine the impact of key macroeconomic determinants identified in the literature as likely drivers of corruption dynamics in open economies. Our analysis of panel data from Eastern European countries (Panel Fully Modified Least Squares) reveals that, in the long run, economic freedom, government expenditure on education, inward foreign direct investment (FDI), and government effectiveness are associated with decreased perceptions of public sector corruption. The findings provide a comprehensive understanding of the macroeconomic drivers of corruption and propose policy recommendations to mitigate its adverse effects on economic growth and equity.

detail.title: Skill, Chance, and the Constitutional Reckoning at the India's Online Gaming Tax War
detail.abstract: The Bengaluru-based company operates an online rummy platform which received a tax demand of ₹21,000 crore for unpaid GST. The figure was staggering, the largest single tax demand in the history of the Indian Republic. The case exceeded normal boundaries because its essential legal foundation established rummy as a gambling activity despite the Supreme Court's 1968 decision that recognized rummy as a skill-based game. 1 Within months, similar demands had been served on Dream11, MPL, A23 Games, PokerBaazi, Junglee Rummy, and dozens of other platforms. The total demands surpassed ₹1.5 lakh crore. Several startups contemplated relocating offshore. The digital entertainment industry in India, which has the fastest expansion rate, generates annual revenues over ₹16,000 crore and experiences a 27% annual growth rate, faced a tax obligation that surpassed their total profits since they started operations. The Gameskraft controversy, according to this paper, represents a different story because it does not involve video games as its main focus. The story shows how an administration that seeks more revenue treats a constitutional boundary as a minor financial problem which they can solve through forceful policing and new law changes. The upcoming Supreme Court judgment which the court will announce after its 8 August 2025 proceedings will determine both tax regulations for a particular industry and the level of legal authority that Indian authorities must show toward their established legal principles.

title: Valuations under Tradeoff Complexity

detail.title: Valuations under Tradeoff Complexity
detail.abstract: Valuation tasks are a workhorse method for testing theories of individual preferences. However, a body of evidence suggests that complexity produces systematic measurement error in valuations, which raises the question of how researchers should interpret and utilize valuation data. To formally study this issue, we develop a model of complexity-driven noise in the valuation of risky prospects, in which the difficulty of comparing options to prices produces systematic noise in their valuations. We show how this model of noise can explain a number of documented valuation patterns that are difficult to rationalize under prevailing theories of risk preferences, as well as novel experimental evidence of systematic inconsistencies across valuation formats. We then characterize which valuation-based tests of preferences are robust to complexity in our model. While complexity distorts the levels of valuations in our model, differences between valuations can be informative, so long as complexity is held fixed across valuation tasks. We provide a formal criterion for robustness and apply it to valuation designs in the literature.

detail.abstract: Tightly coupled systems—financial networks, power grids, epidemic transmission chains—exhibit cascade dynamics in which events occurring in rapid temporal succession show elevated conditional dependence relative to isolated events. Classical empirical conditional probability estimation weights all observations satisfying the conditioning event equally and therefore aggregates cascade-period and quiescent-period observations into a single marginal estimate. We define the cluster-weighted conditional probability p_cluster—the conditional probability of the outcome among observations embedded in dense local activity—as a distinct estimand from the marginal P(A|B), and introduce the Temporally Adaptive Conditional Estimator (TACE) for it. The weighting kernel is derived from a minimal set of axioms with two explicit parametric specifications. We develop a permutation-based test of the null hypothesis H0: p_cluster = P(A|B), demonstrate its calibration via simulation (Type-I error 0.054 at nominal alpha = 0.05 over 2,000 null datasets), and characterize its power as a function of cascade strength and sample size. We propose K-fold cross-validation by held-out predictive log-likelihood for selection of the two tuning parameters. An applied analysis using the complete record of 573 FDIC bank failures from October 2000 through January 2026 yields P_hat_t - P_hat = +0.083 (p = 0.001) for a regional-contagion outcome, with null behavior on non-cascade-coupled discriminant controls. A scan-statistic comparator (Kulldorff 1997) detects the same cascade structure but does not provide the magnitude and directional signal that TACE produces. The estimator is positioned as a complement to classical conditional probability estimation and to existing cascade-detection methods: their joint use yields both the long-run marginal probability and a quantitative, interpretable signal of cluster-induced conditional dependence.

detail.abstract:
Carl Jung's clinical observation — that when an inner situation is not made conscious, it happens outside as fate — has circulated for nearly a century without systematic engagement from behavioral neuroscience. What Jung actually wrote, in Aion (1951, CW 9ii, Para 126), is more precise than the widely circulated paraphrase: "The psychological rule says that when an inner situation is not made conscious, it happens outside, as fate." This paper argues that this authentic proposition finds convergent structural support across four independent research streams developed without reference to each other or to Jung.

The four streams are: Libet's readiness potential experiments (1983), which found that neural precursors of voluntary movement precede reported conscious awareness of intention by an average of 335 milliseconds; LeDoux's dual-pathway threat architecture (1996–2017), which established that subcortical threat-detection circuits can initiate early physiological responses below any threshold of conscious awareness, setting a trajectory toward behavioral expression before cortical processing is complete; Barrett's Theory of Constructed Emotion (2017), which proposes that emotional experience is a predictive construction assembled from prior experience encoded below the level of language, presented to consciousness as unmediated fact; and the Fear Response Gap framework (Anderson, 2021–2026), a practice-derived observational framework independently consistent with these streams, which has theoretically specified a window of approximately 2 to 5 seconds following subcortical cascade initiation as the interval within which conscious somatic intervention may be structurally possible.

Together these streams constitute converging structural support for a mechanistic interpretation of Jung's proposition: the nervous system initiates and justifies behavior through processes the actor cannot access, and the actor encounters the result as fate. The LeDoux-Barrett architecture does not merely provide analogs for Jung's description of the problem — it suggests a specification for the solution. The theoretically derived interception window is proposed as the operational definition of Jung's prescription to make the unconscious conscious: a trainable, neurobiologically grounded interval during which the predictive cascade that would otherwise produce automatic behavioral output may be interruptable through practiced somatic engagement.

Access to the window is proposed to be a dynamic function of body budget status — shaped by relational, developmental, nutritional, and historical conditions — with direct implications for why insight-based therapeutic approaches consistently underperform in populations experiencing cumulative adversity. An additional convergent line is drawn to the Tlingit Shaman's Trail framework, whose practices are structurally consonant with the proposed architecture and constitute a fifth independent observational tradition that appears to have arrived at analogous structural solutions through a completely different epistemological pathway. This paper is a theoretical synthesis and hypothesis-generating framework, not an empirical confirmation paper. Limitations and a four-priority empirical research agenda are specified.

detail.abstract: How do policy rules shape the macroeconomic transmission of commodity-price shocks? We study Brazil's October 2016 shift from administered fuel pricing to import-parity pricing as a discrete institutional change that reallocated oil-price risk away from the sovereign balance sheet. We find that rule-based pricing reduced the amplification of oil shocks through sovereign risk premia and lowered exchange-rate volatility, despite increasing domestic pass-through from global oil prices. The fuel price-sovereign spread relationship changes sharply across regimes: under administered pricing, higher oil prices lower spreads through a commodity-windfall channel, whereas under import-parity pricing the same shock raises spreads on impact as inflationary pressures shift risk onto households and firms. At longer horizons, however, sovereign-risk responses under import-parity pricing weaken and become negative, consistent with lower contingent fiscal exposure and reduced policy uncertainty. Placebo tests, structural breaks, and fuel-versus-nonfuel comparisons support a credibility-based interpretation in which predictable pricing rules limit discretionary intervention and dampen risk-premium amplification.

detail.abstract: Strong future time reference (FTR) languages grammatically mark the future, prompting speakers to mentally separate future events from the present. Using 183,797 firm-year observations collected from 47 countries between 1992 and 2022, we examine the relationship between language FTR and intra-year price discovery. We find that the use of strong-FTR languages is associated with slower incorporation of earnings-relevant information into share prices. The effect is more pronounced for firms with lower analyst coverage and weaker corporate governance. Our findings, which remain robust across extensive sensitivity analyses, have important implications for investors and policymakers.

detail.abstract:
Background. Human-AI interaction has moved from a human-computer interaction research topic to an operational and regulatory concern. The April 2025 rollback of an OpenAI model update after the system became, in the company's own characterisation, overly flattering or agreeable, the March 2026 Science publication demonstrating that sycophantic AI reduces prosocial intentions and promotes dependence, and the August 2026 implementation deadline for European Union AI Act Article 14 human oversight requirements have placed appropriate reliance, calibrated trust, and meaningful oversight at the centre of practitioner and regulatory attention. The literature, however, remains fragmented across disciplines, modalities, and jurisdictions.

Purpose. This paper provides a comprehensive synthesis of human-AI interaction research and practice across three contemporary AI modalities, predictive, generative, and agentic, and integrates this synthesis with the regulatory architectures emerging in the European Union and the Gulf Cooperation Council. The paper is designed as a reference contribution for the wider fifteen-paper slate and as a scholar-practitioner resource for senior cybersecurity, governance, and risk audiences.

Approach. The paper adopts a narrative review methodology combining contemporary 2024 to 2026 empirical literature on trust calibration, appropriate reliance, and oversight effectiveness; primary regulatory document analysis (the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, UAE Information Assurance Standards, UAE Personal Data Protection Law, the UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence, and Saudi Arabian regulatory instruments); and analysis of recent documented incidents including the OpenAI sycophancy rollback and the body of academic work on emergent sycophancy in large language models.

Findings. Three observations emerge from the synthesis. First, the constructs of trust, calibration, and reliance, while conceptually distinct, are increasingly conflated in practitioner discourse; appropriate reliance, the behavioural outcome that practitioner and regulatory frameworks ultimately require, is empirically distinguishable from trust as an attitude and warrants separate measurement. Second, the modality-specific risk profiles differ substantially: predictive AI risks are concentrated in confidence miscalibration and rubber-stamp oversight; generative AI risks are concentrated in sycophancy and anthropomorphic trust manipulation; agentic AI risks are concentrated in oversight tractability as system autonomy increases. Third, the EU AI Act Article 14 oversight architecture is more developed than its GCC counterparts, but GCC regulatory instruments include user awareness, transparency, and cultural appropriateness considerations that EU instruments under-address; cultural bias documented in large language models toward Western entities creates a trust calibration problem in Arabic-speaking user populations that has a limited counterpart in EU deployment contexts.

Implications. Practitioners deploying AI systems across modalities should distinguish trust, calibration, and reliance in their human factors design and assessment. Multi-jurisdictional deployments in the GCC require interaction design that accommodates both EU AI Act oversight obligations and GCC-specific cultural, linguistic, and regulatory expectations. Empirical validation through practitioner vignette surveys is reserved for subsequent research in this slate. Future work will extend the analysis through comparative regulatory mapping (Paper 14) and the assessment of dual-use interaction risks (Paper 12).

title:
No Peasant AI 

On the Coming Enclosure of Cognition, and What Most Societies Have Already Promised to Prevent

detail.title:
No Peasant AI 

On the Coming Enclosure of Cognition, and What Most Societies Have Already Promised to Prevent

detail.abstract: This essay argues that artificial intelligence is best understood not as a tool, a chatbot, or a productivity aid, but as an emerging capability stack: cognitive, conversion, and production infrastructure at once. It helps people learn and reason; it helps them translate thought into the forms by which institutions read them; and it helps them produce the artifacts-code, designs, documents, prototypes, businesses-by which they are recognised and rewarded. If the capability stack is broadly available, AI may become the printing press of capability. If access is tiered by income, employer, school, university, or country, it may instead become a new scribal class-not a wall around books, but a wall around the interpreter, the tutor, the editor, the coder, and the production engine. The argument is not anti-AI. It is the opposite: precisely because AI can expand human agency, the architecture of access matters. Most modern states have, in one form or another, committed themselves to preventing the kind of stratification this essay describes. The piece is written in a diagnostic register. It does not propose a public utility, nor any single implementation model. It argues that the architecture of AI access must not be decided by default-because the architectures that have been decided by default, throughout history, have proven the most difficult to undo. The essay closes with a single testable prediction: the first societies to universalise meaningful AI access will stop wasting as much of their own population. This is a diagnostic essay rather than an empirical study; the empirical citations support specific subclaims, but the central argument is structural.

detail.abstract: American households carry roughly $1.17 trillion in revolving credit card debt and pay annual percentage rates above 21 percent (Federal Reserve, 2024). Those numbers are large, and they receive most of the attention in policy debate and the press. They describe only one half of the credit card economy. The other half is rewards: cash back rates, sign-up bonuses, point earnings, and bundled ancillary benefits, on which issuers compete at least as aggressively as on price. The disclosure regimes in the United States and Canada were designed for the borrowing half. They are largely silent on the rewards half. This paper develops a framework for analyzing the resulting opacity, which I term reward valuation transparency, or RVT. I draw on roughly ten years of structured comparison work covering approximately 250 Canadian credit card products to propose a typology of three RVT failure modes (headline-rate opacity, conditional-value opacity, and comparability opacity) and apply the typology comparatively to the U.S. market. Both markets exhibit RVT failures, though through different mechanisms. The United States produces opacity primarily through reward program complexity and segmentation. Canada produces it primarily through limited statutory comparison infrastructure and concentrated issuer structure. I also identify a meta-RVT problem: the third-party comparison platforms that exist to resolve reward valuation introduce their own opacity through the affiliate compensation that funds them. The paper discusses implications for disclosure regulation, distributive consequences in light of recent evidence that rewards function as a regressive transfer, and the design of consumer-facing comparison tools. The paper does not recommend a specific policy. The choice between regulatory and market-based remedies is treated as an empirical question requiring further work.

title:
The Citizens Standard:
Transition Architecture and Migration Mechanics
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title:
The Citizens Standard:
Transition Architecture and Migration Mechanics
detail.abstract:
The Citizens Standard (Neo-Solon, 2026a) proposes a constitutional monetary architecture whose destination is well-specified. This paper addresses what the architectural paper defers: the path from the current discretionary monetary system to that destination. The central finding is that the Citizens Standard does not require a monetary revolution to begin. Its most powerful mechanism — universal locked equity compounding — can be launched today as a parallel sovereign wealth layer within the existing monetary system, requiring no Federal Reserve replacement, no constitutional amendment, and no banking restructuring at inception.

We specify a five-phase migration architecture in which each phase is self-contained, generates observable evidence, and creates the institutional conditions for the next phase. The phases span approximately 40 to 60 years from launch to full constitutionalization. We then address quantitatively the four hard transition problems the architectural paper acknowledges but does not resolve: existing government debt conversion mechanics, banking separation and credit stability under phased reserve requirements, equity valuation effects of universal systematic ownership flows, and the timing of constitutional lock credibility.

A central quantitative finding concerns the debt transition: a naïve analysis suggests Mode B requires a $2.3 trillion annual primary surplus to stabilize debt/GDP — an apparently impossible fiscal demand. This paper shows that analysis is incomplete. As legacy high-coupon nominal debt rolls to price-indexed instruments over approximately six years, the average sovereign coupon falls from 4.5 percent to approximately 1.0 percent under Mode B, collapsing the interest-growth spread from 3.2 to 0.3 percentage points. A Mode C bridge during Phase 1 and Phase 2, combined with modest fiscal consolidation of approximately 1 percent of GDP over ten years, produces a D/GDP trajectory declining from 127 percent at launch to 84 percent by Year 50 — materially better than the CBO's March 2025 projection of 156 percent by 2055 under current law. International analogues from Chile, Norway, Estonia, and Singapore provide empirical grounding for each phase's feasibility.

title: Measuring the Memory Structure of Intraday Returns: Evidence from E-mini S&P 500 Futures

detail.title: Measuring the Memory Structure of Intraday Returns: Evidence from E-mini S&P 500 Futures
detail.abstract: Standard intraday trading systems treat consecutive returns as approximately independent, ignoring long-range dependence, fractional integration, volatility persistence, and multifractal regime mixing-properties that are measurable and consequential at the one-minute frequency. This paper implements and empirically validates a complete memory-structure measurement toolkit applied to E-mini S&P; 500 (ES) futures on the one-minute timeframe. The toolkit comprises three confidence-weighted Hurst estimators (R/S analysis, aggregated variance, absolute moments), the Geweke-Porter-Hudak (GPH) log-periodogram estimator for the ARFIMA fractional differencing parameter d, a Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (MFDFA) spectrum estimator, and a volatility suite including realized, fractional, and FIGARCH-approximated conditional variance with leverage and jump diagnostics. All components are implemented in MQL5 as a single modular header file suitable for real-time use in indicators, Expert Advisors, and machine learning feature pipelines; the open-source implementation is documented in a companion article series (Brown, 2026a-d). Empirical analysis of 514 New York trading sessions (April 2024-March 2026, approximately 196,000 one-minute observations) yields four principal findings. First, the confidence-weighted Hurst blend produces H = 0.660 (median 0.662)-a strongly upward-biased estimate driven by short-range autocorrelation in the R/S statistic, as predicted by Lo (1991). Second, the GPH estimator, which is robust to this bias, gives pooled d =-0.057 and session-level mean d =-0.006 (SD = 0.121), consistent with near-random-walk behavior. The H-d discrepancy exceeds 0.1 in 75.1% of sessions, directly quantifying the R/S bias in real market data. Third, MFDFA singularity spectrum widths (delta-alpha, Legendre-transformed) average 0.415 (median 0.359), with 44.7% of sessions showing strong multifractal structure, confirming that opposing memory regimes coexist within individual sessions. Fourth, volatility clustering is present but modest at the minute level (mean clustering index 0.071), with jump intensity averaging 0.86%. Together these findings establish that ES M1 intraday returns are near-memoryless in aggregate but heterogeneous in structure, and that the R/S Hurst estimator systematically overstates persistence at this frequency.

title: Taxation, Fiscal Consolidation, and Debt Sustainability in Kenya’s Finance Bills: A Macroeconomic and Theoretical Evaluation

detail.title: Taxation, Fiscal Consolidation, and Debt Sustainability in Kenya’s Finance Bills: A Macroeconomic and Theoretical Evaluation
detail.abstract: This paper examines the macroeconomic implications of Kenya's Finance Bills, with emphasis on taxation structure, fiscal consolidation strategy, and long-run growth and debt sustainability. The analysis situates recent fiscal reforms within Kenya's persistent challenges of rising public debt, weak tax buoyancy, and a structurally narrow formal tax base. It argues that successive Finance Bills have increasingly relied on indirect taxation, digital levies, excise duties, and transactionbased taxes as primary instruments of fiscal consolidation. While such measures support shortterm revenue mobilisation objectives, they may generate contractionary macroeconomic effects in a consumption-driven economy characterised by high informality and liquidity constraints. The paper applies fiscal multiplier theory, the Laffer curve, and standard debt dynamics to evaluate the transmission mechanisms through which taxation affects output and debt sustainability. It finds that tax-induced reductions in disposable income may suppress aggregate demand, weaken private investment, and reduce real GDP growth, thereby offsetting fiscal gains through adverse denominator effects in debt-to-GDP dynamics. In economies with high marginal propensities to consume, these effects are amplified, increasing the likelihood of non-linear output contractions following tax adjustments. The paper further argues that aggressive reliance on distortionary taxation may generate diminishing returns due to behavioural responses and tax base erosion. It concludes by proposing alternative fiscal strategies grounded in international evidence, including compliance-driven base broadening, expenditure-led consolidation, and productivity-enhancing digital tax reforms. The findings suggest that sustainable fiscal adjustment in Kenya requires a balanced approach that integrates revenue mobilisation with growth preservation to avoid selfdefeating debt dynamics.

title: Court Capacity and Crime Deterrence: Evidence from Criminal Court Closures in England and Wales

detail.title: Court Capacity and Crime Deterrence: Evidence from Criminal Court Closures in England and Wales
detail.abstract: This paper shows that criminal court capacity is a key input into crime deterrence, jointly shaping the certainty and celerity of punishment. I exploit large-scale magistrates' court closures in England and Wales between 2010/11 and 2019/20, using a difference-indifferences design with policy switchers and stayers. Court closures increase waiting times for hearings and reduce prosecutorial charging rates. Consistent with these mechanisms, closing 10 percent of courts increases crime by approximately 1.5 crimes per 1,000 population. Theft and violent crime respond in opposite directions, suggesting heterogeneous deterrence effects. The implied social costs far exceed projected fiscal savings.

title: Stochastic market multiple valuation: a peer-panel kernel for firms and portfolios
affiliations: Kozminski University

detail.title: Stochastic market multiple valuation: a peer-panel kernel for firms and portfolios
detail.abstract: Investment funds commit to investors that the portfolio will not breach a stated drawdown threshold with a stated probability over a stated horizon. Translating such a policy into ex-ante compliance measurement is hard with point valuations. This paper develops a probabilistic generalisation of the market multiple method that delivers a density valuation of a firm and aggregates firm-level densities into a portfolio-level distribution suitable for risk-policy compliance. The construction treats the peer panel of N firms, Z quarters and K multiples as a three-dimensional source from which the joint multiple distribution is inferred through decay-weighted marginals coupled by a copula. Combined with target fundamentals it yields a valuation kernel, aggregated across firms into a portfolio kernel. A controlled Monte Carlo shows the kernel beats the conventional peer-median average on accuracy (Diebold-Mariano p < 0.0001), cuts quarter-on-quarter noise by 46 percent, and remains robust under heavy-tailed shocks and loss-making peers.

title: An Interpretable Generative Framework for Pairwise Upstream–Downstream Wind Turbine Power Prediction under Wake Interactions
affiliations: The University of Manchester and The University of Manchester

detail.title: An Interpretable Generative Framework for Pairwise Upstream–Downstream Wind Turbine Power Prediction under Wake Interactions
detail.abstract: Accurate prediction of wake-induced power losses is essential for wind farm performance assessment, particularly for dominant upstream–downstream turbine pairs affected by spacing variation and changing inflow conditions. In practical engineering work flows, such pair-wise interactions are often screened before full-farm simulation, detailed flow modelling, or repowering-related layout assessment. This study develops an interpretable two-stage generative polynomial regression framework for local pair-wise wake-affected wind turbine power prediction. Rather than serving as a global wake solver for full wind-farm wake superposition, the proposed framework is designed as a local wake-aware surrogate for spacing-sensitive downstream power reconstruction. In Stage 1, high-order polynomial models are fitted to SCADA-derived downstream power–angle curves within wind-speed intervals, and the resulting coefficients are extracted as spacing-dependent representations. In Stage 2, coefficient–spacing mappings are used to generate polynomial coefficient sets for unseen pair-wise spacings, enabling downstream power curves to be reconstructed without direct point-wise regression or retraining. Here, the term “generative” refers specifically to coefficient-level curve synthesis under spacing variation. The framework is evaluated using five years of SCADA data from an operational 14-turbine UK wind farm, with 22 turbine pairs used for training and four unseen pairs reserved for validation, including one out-of-range spacing case. Results show that the proposed framework achieves lower prediction errors than Jensen, Frandsen, Bastankhah–Gaussian, MLP, and LSTMbaselines, with average RMSE and MAE values of 57.6 kW and 46.3 kW, respectively. The framework provides a com putationally tractable and interpretable surrogate for rapid pair-wise wake screening, local wake-loss assessment, and engineering pre-evaluation before farm-level analysis.

title: Dynamic Graph Attention Networks for Neuroplasticity-Aware Decoding of Stroke Electroencephalography
affiliations: SSN College of Engineering, SSN College of Engineering and SSN College of Engineering

detail.title: Dynamic Graph Attention Networks for Neuroplasticity-Aware Decoding of Stroke Electroencephalography
detail.abstract: Motor Imagery-based Brain-Computer Interfaces for stroke rehabilitation are limited by non-stationary and asymmetric neural patterns caused by post-stroke cortical reorganization, making static spatial filters ineffective. This work presents a Neuroplasticity-Aware Graph Attention Network (NAGAN) and extends it from subject-specific decoding to calibration-free cross-subject decoding. For subject-specific settings, NAGAN combines multi-scale temporal feature encoding with trial-specific phase-based functional connectivity graphs and achieves aggregate acute-stroke metrics of accuracy 0.8909, kappa 0.7817, and macro-F1 0.8904 under a random 5-subject selection protocol repeated over 5 runs. For cross-subject generalization under Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) evaluation, the framework integrates Riemannian Procrustes Alignment (RPA), a Differentiable Graph Generator (DGG), and Domain Adversarial Neural Network (DANN) adaptation with Gradient Reversal Layer training. Across four datasets, including the Vietnamese UET-175 stroke cohort, the extended pipeline reaches 87.92% LOSO accuracy on Acute Stroke and 75.20% on UET-175 with PLV-initialized adversarial adaptation. These results indicate that combining manifold alignment, learnable topology, and adversarial invariance improves robustness to pathological inter-subject heterogeneity while preserving motor-intent discriminability.

title: SDTD-Seg: Spectral-Domain Dual-Teacher Distillation for Robust Echocardiography Segmentation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Panzhihua University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Panzhihua University

detail.title: SDTD-Seg: Spectral-Domain Dual-Teacher Distillation for Robust Echocardiography Segmentation
detail.abstract: Accurate echocardiography segmentation is a prerequisite for the automated estimation of key cardiac functional metrics, such as Ejection Fraction (EF). However, the widespread presence of speckle noise,signal attenuation, and ambiguous tissue boundaries in ultrasound images poses substantial challenges to existing segmentation models, often resulting in anatomically incoherent false-positive regions and large Hausdorff Distance (HD95) errors. To address these issues, we propose SDTD-Seg, a heterogeneous dual-teacher knowledge distillation framework for robust echocardiography segmentation. Specifically, the framework employs a lightweight yet task-specialized student network built upon a Swin-Tiny encoder, a customized U-Net-like structure-aware decoder with refined skip fusion, and uncertaintyaware prediction, and jointly transfers complementary priors from two frozen teachers, namely DINO and USFM, to capture global semantic structure and ultrasound-specific local texture information. In addition, we introduce a Spectral Stochastic Augmentation Masking (SSAM) strategy in the Fourier domain to expose the student to degraded spectral appearances and promote more robust feature learning. Experimental results on the public CAMUS dataset show that SDTD-Seg achieves a mean Dice score of 0.9083 and an HD95 of 2.68 px under standard inference, demonstrating strong boundaryprecision while preserving competitive overlap accuracy. Moreover, zero-shot evaluation on the external EchoNet-Dynamic dataset suggests promising cross-domain generalization capability, indicating the practical potential of the proposed framework for real-world echocardiography analysis. The source code and pre-trained models are publicly available at https://github.com/imgsd/SDTD-Seg.

title: The Redundancy Trap: Selective Attention and the Trade-off in Belief Updating
affiliations: Yokohama City University, Yokohama City University and Yokohama City University - Graduate School of International Management

detail.title: The Redundancy Trap: Selective Attention and the Trade-off in Belief Updating
detail.abstract: This study examines how households respond to redundancy across information sources and how such redundancy shapes belief updating through a trade-off between precision gains and diminishing returns. We conduct a randomized experiment where half of respondents endogenously choose which and how much information to acquire, while the other half receive information exogenously. Our results reveal three key findings. First, households selectively acquire information rather than observing all available sources, a pattern consistent with limited expected marginal benefits from potentially redundant information. Second, belief updating exhibits diminishing returns as the number of signals increases, indicating that redundancy dominates potential precision gains from observing multiple sources. Third, belief updating is stronger under endogenous choice, suggesting that information is processed more effectively when households optimally allocate attention and information quantity in the absence of perceived redundancy. These findings suggest that accounting for redundancy across information sources is essential for understanding how households optimally acquire and process information, and how belief updating responds to information provision.

title: Multidimensional Energy Poverty in Pakistan: Determinants and Spatial Patterns at the Provincial and District Levels
affiliations: Sukkur IBA University, Students, Sakarya University, Sukkur IBA University, Students, King Saud University, Saudi Arabia and Saveetha University

detail.title: Multidimensional Energy Poverty in Pakistan: Determinants and Spatial Patterns at the Provincial and District Levels
detail.abstract: This paper estimates the Multidimensional Energy Poverty Index (MEPI) for Pakistan and its provinces. It investigates its determinants using data from the most recent rounds of the Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS). The results indicate that 39% of households in Pakistan experience multidimensional energy poverty (MEP). Provincially, the highest prevalence is in Baluchistan (50%), followed by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (48%), Sindh (44%), and Punjab (29%). The likelihood of energy poverty rises with larger household sizes and limited access to water and sanitation facilities. Conversely, it declines with higher educational attainment among the household head and in upper wealth quintiles. Additionally, households receiving remittances are less likely to experience energy poverty. At the provincial level, significant heterogeneity exists in the determinants of MEP. Crucially, energy poverty is more common in rural areas. These findings support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7)-affordable and clean energy-by demonstrating significant disparities across provinces and among vulnerable households. Furthermore, the results align with SDG 6-clean water and sanitation-and SDG 10-reducing inequalities-by emphasizing the crucial roles of water and sanitation facilities, household wealth, and remittances in alleviating energy poverty. The study also advocates for improving educational quality (SDG 4) by emphasizing the positive influence of educational attainment on reducing energy poverty. Finally, it recommends targeted programs and province-specific policy actions to help improve energy access in Pakistan.

title:
How CCyBs Travel? 
Internal Capital Markets & Domestic Borrowing
affiliations: Deutsche Bundesbank - Research Centre, Deutsche Bundesbank, University of Zurich - Department Finance and Deutsche Bundesbank

detail.title:
How CCyBs Travel? 
Internal Capital Markets & Domestic Borrowing
detail.abstract: Macroprudential capital buffers are designed to contain risk inside the activating jurisdiction. We show they do not. Exploiting the staggered activation of countercyclical capital buffers (CCyB) in host countries of German multinationals' foreign subsidiaries, we trace a firmside leakage channel: subsidiary bank credit contracts by 10.6 percent per percentage-point CCyB, while nonbank credit shows no significant response, and German parents replace the lost credit with internal debt. Parents refinance externally at home, raising parent default risk by roughly 25 percent and credit-weighted group default risk by roughly 20 percent of their respective unconditional means. Leverage and risk migrate to the parent's home country, in which no comparable regulation applies.

title: Azerbaijan's Economy in 2026: In the Context of Regional Geo-political Challenges
affiliations: Center for Economic & Social Development (CESD)

detail.title: Azerbaijan's Economy in 2026: In the Context of Regional Geo-political Challenges
detail.abstract: In 2026, the Azerbaijani economy is developing against the backdrop of regional geopolitical tensions, especially the conflict in the Middle East (between Israel-US and Iran) that has virtually closed the Strait of Hormuz, and major disruptions in global energy supplies. These events have led to a sharp increase in global oil prices (Brent averaged 103 USD/barrel in March, spot prices up to 130-150 USD/barrel), inflationary pressures, and a slowdown in world economic growth. According to the IMF's April 2026 World Economic Outlook, in the reference scenario, global growth has fallen to 3.1%, and inflation to 4.4%; in more unfavorable scenarios, growth could fall to 2%, and inflation could rise above 6%. Real GDP growth in Azerbaijan for 2026 is forecast at 2.9% and is expected to reach 134.1 billion manat. The share of the non-oil and gas sector in GDP is expected to approach 75.8%, and in budget revenues-57%. In the first quarter of 2026, GDP amounted to 29.703 billion manat, a decrease of 0.3% compared to the same period last year; a decrease was recorded in the oil and gas sector, and a slight increase in the non-oil and gas sector. State budget revenues in the first quarter exceeded the forecast by 5%, and the share of non-oil and gas revenues reached 57.7%. The article analyzes the trends in GDP, fiscal and export diversification of the economy, assesses sector concentration using the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI), and makes recommendations for increasing resilience to risks posed by regional conflicts. As a result, although the development of the non-oil sector (services, trade, logistics, agro-processing) plays an important role in reducing oil dependence, deeper structural changes in industry and agriculture are necessary.

title: Rethinking the Risk-Free Rate a Swiss-CDS Framework for Emerging Markets
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Rethinking the Risk-Free Rate a Swiss-CDS Framework for Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: The risk-free rate is the foundation of every cost of capital calculation, yet the methods used to estimate it embed errors directly into their design. This paper identifies two such errors and proposes a correction grounded in Damodaran's country risk methodology. The first error is using the US sovereign Credit Default Swap spread as the implicit reference when measuring a country's default risk premium. The US CDS is non-zero, politically volatile, and theoretically inappropriate as a floor. The second error is using rating-agency-based default spreads, which lag market conditions and structurally fail in high-inflation environments. The correction replaces the US CDS reference with the Swiss CDS — the lowest and most structurally stable sovereign CDS globally. The risk-free rate in any local currency becomes: RFR(local) = Local 10Y G-Sec − (Local CDS − Swiss CDS) This requires only three market-observable inputs: the local government bond yield, the local sovereign CDS, and Switzerland's sovereign CDS. No inflation forecasts, no currency conversion, no additional assumptions — because the local government bond yield already embeds all local monetary conditions. All CDS figures are sourced from Damodaran's April 2026 dataset, 10-year CDS Spreads sheet, data as of 31 December 2025. Applied to India, the Swiss-CDS method yields 6.15 percent, compared to 6.55 percent under the conventional US-reference method and 4.91 percent under the rating-based method. The 40- basis-point gap between the Swiss and US references reflects the US 10-year CDS of 0.57 percent against Switzerland's 0.17 percent. The 124-basis-point gap between the CDS-based and rating-based estimates reflects the CDS market's more current view of India's creditworthiness — a divergence Damodaran explicitly documented in his 2024 country risk update.

title: Airbnb and Returns to Housing Capital: Evidence on Inequality from Administrative Data
affiliations: CEREGE, University of La Rochelle, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Nantes - IAE - Department of Business Administration

detail.title: Airbnb and Returns to Housing Capital: Evidence on Inequality from Administrative Data
detail.abstract: This paper examines the distributional implications of Airbnb income using matched administrative data combining transaction-level tourist tax records, cadastral data, and household tax data from the La Rochelle coastal urban area in France. We conceptualize short-term rentals as a mechanism enabling households to extract an intermittent tourist rent from housing assets. Using a Heckman selection model, we distinguish between participation in Airbnb activity and revenues conditional on participation. The results show that higherincome households are more likely to participate in Airbnb hosting, but that higher revenues are driven primarily by price premium rather than rental intensity. This suggests that Airbnb amplifies unequal returns associated with heterogeneous housing assets rather than differences in hosting effort. At the same time, Airbnb income represents a substantial share of disposable income for lower income hosts. The paper highlights the dual role of short-term rentals as both a mechanism reinforcing income concentration and a source of temporary income buffering.

title: Integrating Market Sentiments for Stock Price Prediction: A Comparative Study of Bi-LSTM and Multilayer Perceptions

detail.title: Integrating Market Sentiments for Stock Price Prediction: A Comparative Study of Bi-LSTM and Multilayer Perceptions
detail.abstract: This study investigates the integration of sentiment analysis with machine learning models to forecast stock price movements using the Nvidia Corporation as a case study. Sentiment scores were derived from Nvidia-related financial news headlines using two sentiment analysis tools: FinBERT, a domain-specific tool, and TextBlob, a general-purpose tool. These scores were integrated into predictive frameworks based on bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) networks and multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) developed alongside historical stock price data. This study assesses the predictive performance over the entire observation period and across distinct market phases: bullish, stagnation, and strong bullish conditions. The findings indicate that sentiment features enhance predictive accuracy in specific contexts, particularly during stagnation phases, with TextBlob demonstrating superior performance to FinBERT in specific scenarios. In addition, Bi-LSTM models exhibit consistently superior performance in capturing temporal dependencies compared to MLPs. However, the impact of sentiment features diminished during strongly directional trends, such as those observed in strong bullish markets. The combination of FinBERT and TextBlob in the same dataset allows for a dual-perspective approach to sentiment analysis, thereby providing new insights into the dynamic relationship between market sentiment and stock price behavior. This research contributes to the existing literature on applying sentiment analysis to financial forecasting by advancing the integration of complementary sentiment tools and phase-specific evaluations.

title: Lost Before They Leave: Execution Confidence and the Collapse of Discretionary Travel Demand
affiliations: Glibra Inc

detail.title: Lost Before They Leave: Execution Confidence and the Collapse of Discretionary Travel Demand

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and CEO of Glibra Inc., a technology company developing coordination infrastructure for regional tourism markets. A commercial interest in the domain of this research is declared.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was conducted as an online survey experiment using the Prolific research platform. Participants provided informed consent prior to participation. The study involved no deception, no sensitive personal data collection, and posed no greater than minimal risk. The research was conducted in accordance with ethical standards for online behavioral research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The study was self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract:
Travelers who express genuine interest in small and rural destinations frequently fail to book. Standard demand models-preference assessment, risk perception, motivational readiness cannot explain this failure because it occurs before any of those processes conclude. We introduce Execution Confidence Theory (ECT) to identify the mechanism: in decentralized tourism ecosystems, where lodging, transport, dining, and activities are sourced independently from uncoordinated providers, the anticipated burden of recovering from disruption (restart cost) suppresses commitment before intention crystallizes. We term this state mora -the cognitive suspension of a forward action sequence at an unresolvable institutional node. 
A pre-registered between-subjects experiment (N = 303; osf.io/rznua) tested ECT's central prediction in a winter Finger Lakes travel scenario. Explicit fallback assurance-guaranteeing component substitution without full itinerary reconstruction-produced significantly larger increases in booking commitment (d = +0.32, p = .026) and execution confidence (d = +0.35, p = .015) than coordination bundling alone, while leaving perceived disruption probability unchanged (d =-0.15, p = .301). The restart cost reduction effect (d =-0.66, p < .001) was the strongest finding in the study. Mediation confirmed execution confidence as the operative mechanism (indirect effect = 0.31, 95% CI [0.07, 0.57]). 
These findings reposition recovery infrastructure as a demand-forming mechanism rather than a post-purchase service feature, with direct implications for destination management organizations, booking platforms, and regional tourism cooperative governance. Pre-registration: osf.io/rznua.

title: Field of Education and Political Behavior: Predicting GAL/TAN Voting
